Terms.title: Terms of Use
Terms.effectiveDate: Effective date: June 2026 · Last updated: June 2026

s1.title: 1. Acceptance of Terms
s1.body:
By creating an account or using DPNR ("the Service"), you agree to be bound by these Terms of Use and our Privacy & Data Policy. If you do not agree, do not use the Service.

These terms apply to all users, including free-tier and paid subscribers.

s2.title: 2. Description of Service
s2.body:
DPNR is an AI-assisted personal-development platform. It includes a conversational Companion, structured guided sessions (Decision Room, Mirror Room), a personal Digital Twin that reflects patterns and progress back to you, and a content Library — together helping you explore, reflect on, and act on what matters to you. The Service uses AI language models (currently Anthropic's Claude, via AWS Bedrock) to generate reflections, suggestions, and projections based on content you provide.

The Service is not a mental health service, therapy, or medical advice platform. It is a self-reflective tool. If you are in distress, please seek professional support.

s3.title: 3. Eligibility
s3.body: You must be at least 18 years old to use the Service. By registering, you confirm that you meet this requirement.

s4.title: 4. User Accounts
s4.body:
• You are responsible for maintaining the security of your account credentials.
  • You agree not to share your account with others.
  • You may delete your account at any time from your account settings.
  • We reserve the right to suspend or terminate accounts that violate these terms.

s5.title: 5. Subscriptions and Payments
s5.body:
• Free accounts receive a limited monthly AI token allowance (~3 sessions).
  • Paid plans (Core ₪15/mo, Pro ₪25/mo) are billed monthly via Grow.
  • Subscriptions renew automatically unless cancelled before the renewal date.
  • Refunds are handled on a case-by-case basis — contact support within 7 days of a charge.
  • Prices are inclusive of applicable VAT where required by law.

s6.title: 6. Content You Provide
s6.body:
You retain ownership of all content you submit — your decision narratives, reflections, tags, and journal entries ("User Content").

By using the Service, you grant DPNR a limited, non-exclusive licence to process your User Content solely to:

  • Deliver the Service features (AI responses, storage, display)
  • Generate anonymised, aggregated insights to improve the Service (see Section 7)

We do not sell your personal content or share identified User Content with third parties.

s7.title: 7. Data Use for Service Improvement
s7.body:
To improve the Service's AI quality, product design, and user experience, we may analyse usage patterns and content in anonymised, aggregated form. This means:

  • Anonymisation: Personal identifiers (name, email, account ID) are removed before any analytical use.
  • Aggregation: Insights are derived from patterns across many users — no individual decision narrative is read or attributed.
  • No profiling: We do not build individual user profiles for advertising or third-party sale.
  • AI training: Your content may be used in anonymised form to fine-tune or evaluate our internal AI prompts. We do not share raw User Content with our AI model provider for training purposes beyond standard API usage under that provider's own data terms.

You may opt out of anonymised analytical use by contacting us. Opting out does not affect your ability to use the Service.

s8.title: 8. Prohibited Use
s8.body:
You agree not to:

  • Use the Service to generate harmful, abusive, or illegal content
  • Attempt to reverse-engineer, scrape, or extract AI prompts or model outputs at scale
  • Resell or redistribute the Service without written permission
  • Use automated tools to generate fake decisions or abuse free-tier token limits

s9.title: 9. Disclaimers
s9.body:
• The Service is provided "as is" without warranties of any kind.
  • AI-generated content (reflections, suggestions, projections) is illustrative — it may be inaccurate, incomplete, or not suited to your specific situation. Exercise your own judgement.
  • We do not guarantee uptime, data retention, or AI response quality.

s10.title: 10. Limitation of Liability
s10.body: To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, DPNR shall not be liable for any indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from your use of the Service, including any decisions you make based on AI-generated content.

s11.title: 11. Your Data Rights
s11.body:
You have the right to:

  • Access & Download: Export all your data as a JSON file from your account settings at any time.
  • Delete: Permanently delete your account and all associated data from your account settings. Deletion is irreversible.
  • Correct: Edit your decisions, tags, and reflections directly within the app.
  • Opt out of analytics: Contact us to exclude your data from anonymised analysis.

For requests not handled in-app, email:

s12.title: 12. Changes to These Terms
s12.body: We may update these terms. We will notify you by email or in-app banner at least 14 days before material changes take effect. Continued use after that date constitutes acceptance.

s13.title: 13. Governing Law
s13.body: These terms are governed by the laws of the State of Israel. Disputes shall be resolved in the competent courts of Tel Aviv.

Privacy.title: Privacy & Data Policy
Privacy.effectiveDate: Effective date: June 2026 · Last updated: June 2026

whatWeCollect.title: What We Collect
whatWeCollect.body:
When you use DPNR we collect:

  • Account data: Email address, hashed password (managed via AWS Cognito) or OAuth token, and subscription tier.
  • Your content: Everything you type into the app — Companion conversations, Decision Room narratives and options, Mirror Room reflections, journal check-ins, commitments, and outcomes.
  • Usage data: AI token consumption per session, step completion events, and timestamps.
  • Payment data: Subscription status and billing history. Card details are held exclusively by Grow (our payment processor) — we never store raw card numbers.

anonymisedAnalysis.title: Anonymised Analysis
anonymisedAnalysis.body:
We use anonymised, aggregated data to understand how people use the app and to improve the AI models and prompts. Specifically:

  • All personal identifiers are stripped before analysis.
  • We look at patterns — e.g. which lens types are most used, common emotional themes — never at individual narratives.
  • Aggregated findings may inform product decisions, published research, or AI model improvements.
  • You can opt out by emailing with the subject "Opt out of analytics".

aiProcessing.title: AI Processing
aiProcessing.body:
Your content is sent to Anthropic's Claude models, via AWS Bedrock, to generate reflections and suggestions. This runs under Anthropic and AWS's own commercial API data-use terms, under which your inputs and outputs are not used to train their models.

We do not send your email address or account ID to our AI provider — only the content needed to generate a response, and only for the duration of that request.

dataSharing.title: Data Sharing
dataSharing.body:
We share data only with:

  • Amazon Web Services (AWS) — authentication (Cognito), database and encrypted content storage (DynamoDB), and AI response generation (Bedrock/Anthropic Claude — sent the conversation content needed for that request only)
  • Grow — Israeli payment processing (billing data only)
  • Render — application hosting

We do not sell personal data to third parties.

dataRetention.title: Data Retention
dataRetention.body:
• Your decisions and reflections are retained for as long as your account is active.
  • When you delete your account, all personal data is permanently deleted within 30 days.
  • Anonymised, aggregated analytics data (no personal identifiers) may be retained indefinitely.
  • Payment records are retained for 7 years as required by Israeli accounting law.

yourRights.title: Your Rights
yourRights.body:
Under applicable data protection law you have the right to:

  • Access: See all data we hold about you (use "Download my data" in account settings)
  • Portability: Export your data as machine-readable JSON
  • Erasure: Delete your account and all associated data (use "Delete my account" in account settings)
  • Correction: Edit your decisions and reflections directly in the app
  • Restriction: Ask us to pause processing while a dispute is resolved
  • Objection: Opt out of legitimate-interest processing (analytics)

To exercise rights not covered in-app:

security.title: Security
security.body: All data is encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest. Your personal content — decisions, reflections, journal entries, and conversations — is additionally protected with per-user application-level encryption: each account has its own encryption key, wrapped under your password (and a one-time recovery code) using AWS KMS. That key is only ever unwrapped, server-side, for a limited window tied to your own session or a feature you've enabled (such as a Daily Card or Weekly Recap) — never held decrypted at rest or kept available indefinitely. This is not end-to-end encryption in the sense that only your device can ever read your content: our systems can and do decrypt it, briefly, to do the processing those features require. We never store your password in plain text, and if you lose both your password and your one-time recovery code, this content cannot be recovered by us or anyone else — there is no backend override.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: We use a session cookie to keep you signed in, alongside authentication tokens (issued by AWS Cognito) held in your browser. We do not use tracking or advertising cookies.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: We'll notify you by email at least 14 days before any material change to this policy.

choice.label: A moment to stay

choice.body: There's no right pace here. You can go a little deeper, or continue. Both are fine.

deeper.label: A little deeper
deeper.hint: Everything here is optional. Write as much or as little as you like, or just notice what comes. What you write is private and only shapes your closing reflection.

underneath.title: Is there something quieter underneath that feeling?
underneath.body: Sometimes anger is covering hurt, or worry is covering care. Take a moment with whatever is there.

payoff.title: What did that reaction protect you from, or give you, in that moment?
payoff.body: Even a reaction that costs you something is usually trying to help.

belief.title: What did this moment seem to say about you?

stepInfo.1: Naming your decision clearly is the first step toward making it with intention rather than reacting to it.
stepInfo.2: Writing out both real options, even roughly, turns a foggy dilemma into something you can actually compare.
stepInfo.3: Emotions often show up in the body before the mind can name them. Noticing where helps you trust what you're feeling.
stepInfo.4: Different lenses surface different truths. Pick the one that matches what feels most alive in this decision right now.
stepInfo.5: Sit with each option honestly. The goal isn't to talk yourself into one, it's to see both clearly.
stepInfo.6: Values and needs are usually what a decision is really about, underneath the practical details.
stepInfo.7: Imagining a year ahead helps surface a gut sense of direction that pure logic sometimes misses.
stepInfo.8: This is a chance to see the whole shape of what you explored, before moving toward a next step.
stepInfo.9: An outside reflection of your own process can surface a thread you didn't consciously connect yourself.
stepInfo.10: A next step only has to be small enough to actually happen. Momentum matters more than size.

stepReflections.1: Naming what you're carrying is the first act of clarity.
stepReflections.2: Every decision holds two truths, and this step helps you see both.
stepReflections.3: Your body often knows what your mind is still working out.
stepReflections.4: The lens you choose shapes what becomes visible.
stepReflections.5: Looking closely at each path, without rushing, is wisdom.
stepReflections.6: What you value most is the compass behind every real choice.
stepReflections.7: Imagining forward helps you feel which path is truly yours.
stepReflections.8: Seeing the whole picture helps you understand what you truly know.
stepReflections.9: What you discovered here belongs to you. Carry it with care.
stepReflections.10: A small step taken with intention is worth more than a leap taken in fear.

affirmations.0: You showed up for yourself today. That takes real courage.
affirmations.1: Every decision made with awareness is a step toward your truest self.
affirmations.2: Clarity is a gift you've given yourself today.
affirmations.3: You did the inner work. That matters more than you know.
affirmations.4: Slowing down to listen to yourself is never time wasted.
affirmations.5: The courage to look within is the beginning of all wisdom.
affirmations.6: You chose to understand yourself better. That is everything.

info.1: Naming exactly what happened — without judgment — is the first step to seeing it clearly.
info.2: Your thought, feeling, body sensation, and reaction usually arrive together, faster than you can think. Slowing down to name each one separately is where insight starts.
info.3: How you coped afterward, and whether this keeps happening with the same people or situations, is often more revealing than the incident itself.
info.4: Every reaction ripples outward — into your energy, your mood, and the parts of your life it actually touches.
info.5: Seeing the whole arc reflected back can surface a thread you didn't consciously connect yourself.
info.6: A commitment only has to be small enough to actually happen.

reflections.1: What you name clearly, you can finally look at.
reflections.2: Your body often knows before your mind finds the words.
reflections.4: Nothing that affects you is really "just in your head."
reflections.5: Reflection is how experience becomes understanding.
reflections.6: A small, honest step is worth more than a perfect plan.

peoplePleasing.name: People-Pleasing
peoplePleasing.meaning: Prioritizing approval, harmony or another person's comfort over one's own needs, truth or boundaries.
peoplePleasing.showsUp: You might notice it when a yes comes out before you've checked what you actually want.

avoidance.name: Avoidance
avoidance.meaning: Pulling away, delaying, distracting or disengaging when something feels difficult, uncertain or exposing.
avoidance.showsUp: You might notice it when a hard conversation, message or decision keeps sliding to later.

overControl.name: Over-Control
overControl.meaning: Trying to reduce uncertainty by tightly managing outcomes, timing, details, people or the environment.
overControl.showsUp: You might notice it when plans change and you feel a pull to take everything back into your own hands.

perfectionism.name: Perfectionism
perfectionism.meaning: Rigid standards that can turn 'good enough' into something unsafe, incomplete or unacceptable.
perfectionism.showsUp: You might notice it when something is finished but still doesn't feel safe to share.

overResponsibility.name: Over-Responsibility
overResponsibility.meaning: Taking emotional or practical responsibility for things that may not fully belong to the user.
overResponsibility.showsUp: You might notice it when someone else's mood or problem starts to feel like yours to fix.

emotionalSuppression.name: Emotional Suppression
emotionalSuppression.meaning: Minimizing, intellectualizing or pushing away feelings instead of allowing them to be noticed and processed.
emotionalSuppression.showsUp: You might notice it when you explain a feeling away, or say "I'm fine", before letting yourself feel it.

conflictAvoidance.name: Conflict Avoidance
conflictAvoidance.meaning: Avoiding disagreement or difficult conversations in order to preserve safety, harmony or acceptance.
conflictAvoidance.showsUp: You might notice it when you swallow a disagreement to keep the peace.

hyperIndependence.name: Hyper-Independence
hyperIndependence.meaning: Reluctance to ask for help, rely on others or show need because dependence feels uncomfortable or unsafe.
hyperIndependence.showsUp: You might notice it when help is offered and something in you says you'll manage alone.

reassuranceSeeking.name: Reassurance Seeking
reassuranceSeeking.meaning: Repeatedly looking outside oneself for confirmation, approval or certainty when internal confidence feels unstable.
reassuranceSeeking.showsUp: You might notice it when you check again, or ask again, to feel sure it's okay.

withdrawal.name: Withdrawal
withdrawal.meaning: Becoming quiet, distant or unavailable when emotionally activated.
withdrawal.showsUp: You might notice it when you go quiet or slip away just as things become emotional.

overthinking.name: Overthinking
overthinking.meaning: Repeated analysis used to seek certainty, prevent mistakes or avoid emotional exposure.
overthinking.showsUp: You might notice it when you replay a conversation, or run through every outcome, to feel ready.

selfAbandonment.name: Self-Abandonment
selfAbandonment.meaning: Ignoring one's own needs, truth or limits to preserve connection or avoid rejection or conflict.
selfAbandonment.showsUp: You might notice it when your own need gets set aside so the connection stays smooth.

fearBasedProcrastination.name: Fear-Based Procrastination
fearBasedProcrastination.meaning: Delay driven by risk, exposure, possible failure, judgment or uncertainty.
fearBasedProcrastination.showsUp: You might notice it when something that matters keeps waiting until it feels less risky.

angerAsProtection.name: Anger as Protection
angerAsProtection.meaning: Anger may sometimes appear alongside hurt, fear, powerlessness, shame or a boundary violation. Treat this as a possibility, never an assumed cause.
angerAsProtection.showsUp: You might notice it when anger arrives quickly, and something softer may be sitting underneath it.

fixingRescuing.name: Fixing / Rescuing
fixingRescuing.meaning: Moving quickly to solve, manage or rescue others instead of staying with one's own experience and allowing shared responsibility.
fixingRescuing.showsUp: You might notice it when you jump in with solutions before staying with what you feel.

testingPushingAway.name: Testing / Pushing Away
testingPushingAway.meaning: Creating distance, conflict or tests to check whether another person will stay, care or respond.
testingPushingAway.showsUp: You might notice it when you create distance to see whether someone will come closer.

overAccommodation.name: Over-Accommodation
overAccommodation.meaning: Changing oneself excessively to fit an environment, relationship or expectation.
overAccommodation.showsUp: You might notice it when you reshape yourself around what a room or a person seems to expect.

freezeShutdown.name: Freeze / Shutdown
freezeShutdown.meaning: Reduced access to words, action or decision-making when the system feels overwhelmed.
freezeShutdown.showsUp: You might notice it when words, choices or action suddenly feel out of reach.

comparison.name: Comparison
comparison.meaning: Using other people as the main reference point for worth, success, progress or identity.
comparison.showsUp: You might notice it when someone else's progress changes how you feel about your own.

selfCriticism.name: Self-Criticism
selfCriticism.meaning: Turning discomfort, mistakes or vulnerability into internal judgment or attack.
selfCriticism.showsUp: You might notice it when a small mistake turns into a harsh voice inside.

pushPullApproachAvoidance.name: Push-Pull / Approach-Avoidance
pushPullApproachAvoidance.meaning: Wanting closeness, success or change while also pulling away when it becomes emotionally real.
pushPullApproachAvoidance.showsUp: You might notice it when something you want comes closer and part of you starts to step back.
